investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: plain curl GETs (descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser) of the venue's own official events list page (https://quasimodo.club/en/events) and one event detail page. Both are WordPress-rendered static HTML with clean, consistently-structured event markup (date/time/title/tags/ticket-link on the list; full date/start/door-time/price on the detail page). No JSON-LD Event data, EventON, Tribe Events, Fourvenues, or Sanity signal was present — only generic Yoast SEO WebPage/Organization schema. No structural/browser escalation was needed to answer the investigation question.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://quasimodo.club/en/events (200 OK, 119,311 bytes) returned 29 consistently-structured static HTML <li class="event-item"> cards, each with a full date+time ('04.09.2026 - 22:00'), title, genre tags, and a permalink URL. A follow-up curl GET of one event detail page (https://quasimodo.club/en/events/blues-caravan-3-7229, 200 OK, 92,532 bytes) confirmed the same event's full date ('25. September 2026'), start time, door time, and a presale price ('ab 30€ plus fee'). This directly answers the investigation question at Level 1 — no escalation to Level 2/3 was needed.

venue_reference: Quasimodo (jazz/live-music club, Charlottenburg, Berlin — Kantstraße 12A, in the basement of the former Delphi Filmpalast)

identity.notes: The bare domain quasimodo.de is NOT the club's own programme site — it is retained (ev-identity) as a splash/landing page ('Willkommen im Quasimodo / Bitte wählen Sie') that itself links out to quasimodo.club ('Club'), quasimodo.bar ('Bar'), and an external event-location listing. quasimodo.club/en/ is confirmed as the venue's own official programme site directly from its own retained Yoast SEO WebPage schema name field: 'Quasimodo Club Berlin - Kantstraße 12A, 10623 Berlin' — matching the address independently reported by third-party discovery sources (visitBerlin.de, Berlin.de, Wikipedia) for the Quasimodo jazz club in Charlottenburg.

site_classification.platform: WordPress 7.1 (Yoast SEO for generic page schema only). A custom 'events' post type renders clean, consistently-structured static HTML event cards on the events list page and a richer static HTML detail block (date/start/door-time/price/ticket-link) on each event's own detail page. No EventON, Tribe Events Calendar, Fourvenues widget, or Sanity signal is present anywhere in the retained HTML.

title.value: e.g. 'Marcos Coll – Album Release Concert' (list page's own <h4 class="event-title">; also the detail page's own <h1>)
title.notes: Directly stated per event on both the list page and the detail page.

start_date.value: e.g. '04.09.2026 - 22:00' (list page's own <div class="date">, visible-xs variant); also '25. September 2026' + 'Start: 22:00' on the detail page
start_date.notes: The list page's own 'visible-xs' date div states the FULL date (day.month.year) plus time directly per event card — no month/year heading combination is needed, unlike some other sources this project has investigated. The detail page independently confirms the same full date in a different format ('25. September 2026') plus a separate 'Start:' time row. Timezone is not explicitly stated (assume Europe/Berlin local, floating).

time.value: e.g. 22:00 (list page's own <div class="time">; detail page's own 'Start:' table row)
time.notes: Directly stated per event; the detail page additionally distinguishes 'Start:' (22:00) from 'Einlass:' (door/entry time, e.g. 20:30) — a useful extra distinction not present on the list page.

end.notes: No end time or end date is present anywhere in the retained list-page or detail-page evidence.

venue_location.notes: Not present per-record on either the list page or the sampled detail page (no venue name/address is repeated on individual event cards or detail pages). This source resolves to exactly ONE physical venue via source_id (Quasimodo, Kantstraße 12A — confirmed separately in ev-identity), matching this project's existing Razzmatazz/Jamboree precedent for a single-venue source that does not restate its own venue name per event.

source_record_id.value: the event's own permalink slug under https://quasimodo.club/en/events/{slug}/ (e.g. 'blues-caravan-3-7229', where the trailing number appears to be the underlying WordPress post ID)
source_record_id.notes: No bare numeric id is exposed as its own labelled field, but each event's own href/canonical URL is the site's own permanent permalink under /en/events/{slug}/ — the same documented judgement already established for Moog Barcelona, A-Trane, and LAV (a permalink URL slug the source itself uses as its own canonical path satisfies the stable identifier rule). The trailing numeric suffix visible in every slug (e.g. '-7229', '-7384', '-7387') is consistent with an underlying WordPress post ID, but its stability was not independently proven via repeated fetch in this investigation, so it is noted only as a secondary observation.

event_url.notes: Directly stated as the list card's own <a href> and confirmed as the detail page's own <link rel="canonical">.

price.value: e.g. 'ab 30€ (plus fee)' (detail page's own 'Presale:' table row — an approximate/starting price, not a fixed single amount)
price.notes: Present only on the detail page (not the list page), directly stated as-is including the source's own 'ab' ('from'/starting-price) qualifier and separate '(plus fee)' note — retained honestly as the source's own approximate text, not converted into a single fabricated numeric price.

reasons: Identity PROVEN directly from retained evidence, including an explicit check ruling out the bare .de domain as a mere splash page.
acquisition_class STATIC_HTML, a resolved supported class, retained at Level 1 with no escalation needed.
Two CONFIRMED public data paths retained: the events list page (29 real upcoming events) and one representative event detail page.
title and start_date both PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE — the list page states a full date+time per event card, no contextual combination needed.
source_record_id PROVEN via the documented URL-slug strategy already established for Moog Barcelona/A-Trane/LAV.

recommended_family STATIC_EVENT_LIST — an existing collector family this project already documents (list page enumerates events + links; a per-event detail fetch adds price/door-time). No fundamentally new acquisition pattern required.

Held at READY_FOR_OFFLINE_PROOF rather than READY_FOR_ACTIVATION because this investigation deliberately did not write or run an offline DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION parser/test against the retained fixtures — that offline-proof/collector-wiring step is explicitly out of scope for this investigation task and is left as separate follow-up work, per gate 9 in docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md.

Re-verified live on 2026-08-26 (plain curl GET, descriptive User-Agent, no auth/browser): the events list page still returns the same 29 real, consistently-structured event cards (200 OK, 119,909 bytes) and the sampled 'Blues Caravan' detail page still returns the same date/start/door-time/presale-price block (200 OK, 92,732 bytes) — both retained byte-faithfully as new evidence (ev-events-page-reverify, ev-event-detail-reverify) and as fixtures/quasimodo-berlin/*.html for offline testing. A real, dependency-free, no-network offline test suite (tests/quasimodo.test.mjs) now re-parses these retained fixtures and reproduces the exact claimed title/date/time/source_record_id/price/door-time values deterministically, satisfying gate 9. Advanced from READY_FOR_OFFLINE_PROOF to READY_FOR_ACTIVATION.
